samples.summary: The todo file marks '.claude/commands/self-review.md' as delivered ([x]), and CLAUDE.md/CONTRIBUTING.md (already on this branch) tell every contributor to run `/self-review` to drive the bounded review loop, but no such file exists anywhere in the repository (no `.claude/commands/` directory at all, and it is not gitignored — only `.claude/settings.local.json` is). If the command file genuinely was never added, the entire workflow this PR documents is unusable as written: an agent following CLAUDE.md step 3 or CONTRIBUTING.md's PR workflow would invoke a command that does not exist.
samples.evidence: Todo item: '- [x] `.claude/commands/self-review.md` — drives the bounded loop from any branch, no handoff, no `agent/` prefix, no cloud ownership.' Checked with `Glob '.claude/commands/*.md'` and `Glob '.claude/**'` — both returned no files; `.gitignore` does not exclude `.claude/commands/`.

samples.summary: The lessons file's third entry says the fix was to 'name the invocable tool for the agent path and mark the rest as "ask the human"', implying `/code-review` and `/simplify` were removed from the agent-facing rotation. CLAUDE.md step 3 (already on this branch) still names both `/code-review` and `/simplify` directly in the rotation description ('2 design fit + `superpowers:requesting-code-review`, ... /code-review or /simplify depends on its harness'), which is consistent with the stated fix (mark as conditional, ask if unavailable) but the lesson's framing ('put /code-review and /simplify in the round rotation... a locked door') could read as though they were removed rather than annotated as conditional.

verdict.reason: I independently verified the absence claim rather than trusting the reviewer's account. A full recursive listing of the repository (Glob "*" and Glob ".*", which both returned deeply-nested results proving the tool traverses the whole tree, not just the top level) contains no `.claude` directory anywhere — not at the repo root, not under `.trusted/` (the mirrored trusted-scripts tree), nowhere. Targeted globs (`.claude/**`, `**/.claude/**`, `.trusted/.claude/**`, `**/self-review.md`) all return zero matches. `.gitignore` (read in full) excludes only `.claude/settings.local.json`, so nothing hides a real `.claude/commands/` directory from git. The working tree's HEAD (`.git/HEAD` = `6dcc9efac9d21d57a4629a67c71896c58a876dac`) is exactly the tip of `refs/remotes/origin/feat/self-review-loop`, i.e. this IS the branch the todo file describes, at its final state — there is no later commit that could still add the file. Meanwhile the prose genuinely claims delivery and depends on the file: `docs/tasks/active/20260917-self-review-loop-todo.md:70` checks off '`.claude/commands/self-review.md` — drives the bounded loop from any branch'; `CONTRIBUTING.md:185` tells contributors '`/self-review` drives it'; `docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md:57` lists 'Self review | `/self-review` — `.claude/commands/self-review.md`' in its table. All three point at a file that is not in the working tree. This is a straightforward instance of 'documentation contradicted by this PR's own code' (here, the missing artifact standing in for code): the todo file's own checkbox is falsified by the repository state, and CONTRIBUTING.md/the design doc direct a reader (human or agent) to a slash command that cannot be invoked. I found no counterexample after an exhaustive search, so there is no refutation ground to cite.
